objective: Introduce a survey-neutral, explicit light-curve normalization contract and align product documentation without changing the frozen scientific model baseline.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The product roadmap requires separation of import support, analysis support, model compatibility, and scientific validation.
PR #212 introduces explicit source-column mapping and declared time/measurement semantics; it does not implement end-to-end external survey adapters or establish cross-survey model performance.
The v0.2.0 42-feature contract and v1.0.1 release artifacts must remain unchanged.

baseline.description: Main branch and published release v1.0.1; frozen scientific baseline v0.2.0.

expected_improvement: Preserve source-row identity, order, duplicate observations, missing numeric values, units, time semantics, and declared measurement type during normalization.
Reject ambiguous or malformed mappings without silently converting units, flux/magnitude, or time systems.
Add regression coverage for reordered/renamed columns, missing values, malformed inputs, duplicate observations, and no implicit conversions.
Keep import normalization distinct from model compatibility and scientific validation.

findings: Every meaningful implementation change requires a lifecycle record in the same pull request.
Schema normalization must preserve explicit units and time semantics and must not silently imply model compatibility.
CI success is not scientific acceptance; source-backed cross-survey inference remains unimplemented and unvalidated.

open_blockers: Verify normalization regression tests, runtime smoke tests, package build, and dependency audit.
Implement and validate at least one source-backed external-survey adapter and compatible analysis path before making cross-survey capability claims.
Rerun and inspect current-head CI after correcting the lifecycle decision enum.

knowledge_carried_forward: Keep the v0.2.0 baseline and v1.0.1 release immutable.
Do not claim end-to-end multi-survey support or cross-survey model performance from schema normalization alone.
